target_name: Capacity growth funded by total external finance
rationale: The construct is internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a one-component extension of the archive's gen-6 "Capacity growth funded by outside equity" (which already delivered fmb −3.77 with zero alpha) and the conditioner is essentially the published net-external-financing anomaly, so adding the debt leg is unlikely to address the diagnosed alpha failure rather than merely rescale the same slope.

target_name: Capacity growth with thin slack and inventory overhang
rationale: This is the third pairwise recombination of the same three conditioners (funding gap, solvency slack, inventory glut) around the identical ppegt-growth carrier already tested in gens 5–8, so despite correct sign construction and a legitimate coverage motive it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Inventory building into an existing overhang
rationale: Economically coherent and internally consistent with both legs on the same (inventory) channel and dense inputs, though the two legs are mechanically correlated — building inventory raises invt/sale — so the interaction risks approximating a squared version of the known inventory-growth anomaly rather than a true conditional.

Gross PPE almost never declines, so INDICATOR(GROWTH(ppegt,1),0) is near-constant at 1 and the "joint-state" count collapses to the deficit-year count already tested in gen 4 ("Capacity growth with chronic deficit years"), undermining the claimed novelty.

target_name: Capacity growth with confirmed uses and sources shortfall
rationale: Signs and construction are consistent and the noise-reduction rationale is a genuinely different argument from earlier multi-risk merges, but the sources–uses accounting identity makes the two legs near-mechanical duplicates (differing mainly by cash and non-cash items), so the incremental information beyond the existing leader is likely modest and coverage remains oancf-constrained.

target_name: Hiring commitments with thin solvency slack
rationale: A defensible generality test — swapping the flow funding gap for the dense balance-sheet slack state on the validated labor carrier — with correct sign and better expected coverage, though it remains a recombination of two already-tested components and the base leg is the known employee-growth anomaly.
